pairs: ut David reverteretur a cæde Amalec,
David returned from the slaughter of Amalek,
et maneret in Siceleg duos dies.
and he remained for two days at Ziklag.
In die autem tertia apparuit homo veniens de castris Saul veste conscissa, et pulvere conspersus caput: et ut venit ad David, cecidit super faciem suam, et adoravit.
Then, on the third day, a man appeared, arriving from the camp of Saul, with his garments torn and dust sprinkled on his head. And when he came to David, he fell on his face, and he reverenced.
“I have fled from the camp of Israel.”
Quod est verbum quod factum est?
“What is the word that has happened?
“The people have fled from the battle,
et multi corruentes e populo mortui sunt:
and many of the people have fallen and died.
sed et Saul et Jonathas filius ejus interierunt.
Moreover, Saul and his son Jonathan have passed away.”
Dixitque David ad adolescentem qui nuntiabat ei:
And David said to the youth who was reporting to him,
Unde scis quia mortuus est Saul,
and his son Jonathan have died?”
Et ait adolescens qui nuntiabat ei:
And the youth, who was reporting it to him,
said: “I arrived by chance on mount Gilboa.
et Saul incumbebat super hastam suam:
And Saul was lying upon his spear.
porro currus et equites appropinquabant ei,
Then the chariots and horsemen drew near to him.
For anguish has taken hold of me,
et adhuc tota anima mea in me est.
and still my whole life is in me.”
sciebam enim quod vivere non poterat post ruinam:
For I knew that he was not able to live after the fall.
et tuli diadema quod erat in capite ejus,
And I took the diadem that was on his head,
and the bracelet from his arm,
et attuli ad te dominum meum huc.
and I have brought them here to you, my lord.”
Apprehendens autem David, vestimenta sua scidit,
Then David, taking hold of his garments,
omnesque viri qui erant cum eo,
tore them, with all the men who were with him.
et jejunaverunt usque ad vesperam super Saul,
and fasted until evening, over Saul and over his son Jonathan,
et super Jonathan filium ejus, et super populum Domini,
and over the people of the Lord and over the house of Israel,
et super domum Israël, eo quod corruissent gladio.
because they had fallen by the sword.
Dixitque David ad juvenem qui nuntiaverat ei:
And David said to the youth who had reported it to him,
Filius hominis advenæ Amalecitæ ego sum.
“I am the son of a man who is a new arrival from the Amalekites.”
Quare non timuisti mittere manum tuam ut occideres christum Domini?
“Why were you not afraid to put forth your hand, so that you would kill the Christ of the Lord?”
Vocansque David unum de pueris suis,
And calling one of his servants,
and rush against him” And he struck him,
“Your blood is upon your own head.
os enim tuum locutum est adversum te,
For your own mouth has spoken against you,
‘I have killed the Christ of the Lord.’”
Planxit autem David planctum hujuscemodi super Saul,
Then David mourned a lamentation over Saul and over his son Jonathan,
(et præcepit ut docerent filios Juda arcum,
(And he instructed that they should teach the sons of Judah the bow,
sicut scriptum est in libro justorum),
just as it is written in the Book of the Just.)
on behalf of those who are dead,
Inclyti Israël super montes tuos interfecti sunt:
The illustrious of Israel have been killed upon your mountains.
How could the valiant have fallen?
Do not choose to announce it in Gath,
and do not announce it in the crossroads of Ashkelon. Otherwise,
the daughters of the Philistines may rejoice; otherwise,
the daughters of the uncircumcised may exult.
nec pluvia veniant super vos, neque sint agri primitiarum:
nor rain fall over you, and may these not be the fields of the first-fruits.
quia ibi abjectus est clypeus fortium:
For in that place, the shield of the valiant was cast away,
as if he had not been anointed with oil.
From the blood of the slain,
from the fat of the strong,
the arrow of Jonathan never turned back,
et gladius Saul non est reversus inanis.
and the sword of Saul did not return empty.
in morte quoque non sunt divisi:
even in death they were not divided.
qui vestiebat vos coccino in deliciis,
who clothed you with scarlet finery,
qui præbebat ornamenta aurea cultui vestro.
who offered ornaments of gold for your adornment.
How could the valiant have fallen in battle?
Jonathas in excelsis tuis occisus est?
How could Jonathan have been slain on the heights?
and worthy to be loved above the love of women.
Sicut mater unicum amat filium suum,
As a mother loves her only son,
so also did I love you.
How could the robust have fallen,
and the weapons of war have perished?”
